The test image shows a tomato plant with:
- A central bleached/tan, cracked, collapsed stem
- Extensive brown desiccated/dead leaves throughout
- Plant has clearly wilted and collapsed
- Stem appears bleached, hardened, and cracked

Affected part: **stem**. Top candidates: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.

Now reading one reference per candidate class:
Sclerotinia reference: bleached/tan stem with dark sclerotia visible, black plastic mulch background - very similar to the test image. Strong match.
Southern_Blight reference: shows internal stem tissue, not matching well with test image appearance.
Alternaria reference: dark blackish-brown canker - doesn't match the bleached/tan appearance of the test image stem.

This second Sclerotinia reference confirms the diagnosis: bleached/tan cracked stem with large black sclerotia embedded in the tissue, leading to plant collapse.

**Summary of evidence:**

- Test image shows a bleached/tan, cracked, hardened stem with what appears to be a dark spot (sclerotium) at top, surrounded by completely wilted, brown dead leaves, with black plastic mulch in background.
- Sclerotinia Bugwood_21 reference: identical bleached stem at soil level with dark sclerotia, same black plastic mulch context.
- Sclerotinia Bugwood_4 reference: cut stem reveals white bleached tissue with large black sclerotia — hallmark of Sclerotinia timber rot.
- Southern_Blight: showed internal stem cut — less consistent with overall test image.
- Alternaria: dark black canker, not bleached — doesn't match.
